acceptance_criteria.criterion: npm run build-personas succeeds with three targets.
Output directories contain files for all three targets.

summary: Added 'deep-agents' as a third build target in ai-insights/personas/persona-build.config.js: new FRONTMATTER_DA constant using {{id}} + {{cc_description}} for minimal frontmatter; targets array ['vscode','claude-code','deep-agents']; outputDirs entry for both ledger and standalone suites.
Added da_file_name field to all 9 ledger persona YAMLs (1-planner.md through 9-synthesis.md), mirroring the cc_file_name naming pattern.
Build verified: 81 files written (27 ledger + 54 standalone across 3 targets). Check mode passes cleanly. Deep-agents output contains only name + description frontmatter fields.

comments.note: The config-level FRONTMATTER_DA uses {{id}} for the name field (e.g. 'ledger-3-dev') rather than the roster-derived human-friendly title. This is intentional for deep-agents/LangGraph machine consumers, but future persona template authors should document this convention in personas/docs/ to avoid confusion with the VS Code and Claude Code templates that use human-readable names.

The 6-reviewer.yaml has id: ledger-5-reviewer (a numbering anomaly — matches CUD pattern from when security-auditor was added later). This pre-existing inconsistency does not affect the build but would be worth correcting in a housekeeping pass.

summary: AC1 PASS: `node scripts/build-personas.js --check` and `--check --strict` both succeed with 81 personas processed, no errors.
AC2 PASS: All 6 output directories populated — ledger (9+9+9) and standalone (18+18+18) across vs-code, claude-code, and deep-agents targets = 81 total.
AC3 PASS: Every deep-agents file (27 total: 9 ledger + 18 standalone) contains exactly 2 frontmatter fields (name + description). No other metadata leaks through.
AC4 PASS: All 9 ledger persona YAMLs have da_file_name using the N-<role-slug>.md pattern, consistent with cc_file_name. Filenames in output match da_file_name values.
Regression PASS: Existing vs-code and claude-code targets produce unchanged, correct output.
Edge case confirmed: Standalone deep-agents files use content-basename filenames (e.g. developer.md) since no da_file_name added to standalone YAMLs — intentional per WP scope.
Pre-existing ID anomaly noted (ledger-5-reviewer, ledger-6-docs, ledger-7-synthesis in personas 6, 8, 9) — flagged by Developer, pre-dates this WP, does not affect build correctness.

comments.note: Pre-existing ID anomaly: personas/ledger/src/meta/6-reviewer.yaml has id: ledger-5-reviewer, 8-documentation.yaml has id: ledger-6-docs, 9-synthesis.yaml has id: ledger-7-synthesis. The deep-agents `name` field is derived from {{id}}, so these personas appear with non-sequential IDs to deep-agents consumers (e.g. name: ledger-5-reviewer for the 6th persona). This is pre-existing debt; da_file_name values correctly use sequential numbering regardless. Worth a housekeeping pass to align IDs with sequence numbers.

Standalone deep-agents persona `developer.md` has name: developer-standalone, while all others follow the pattern standalone-<slug>. This is because the developer standalone persona has a non-standard id. Consistent with existing behavior, no change needed in this WP.

summary: Reviewed persona-build.config.js, all 9 ledger persona YAMLs, and representative deep-agents generated output. No blocking issues found.
FRONTMATTER_DA constant is clean, minimal, and well-commented — correctly explains the dual cc_description resolution path (ledger plugin roster vs. standalone description field).
outputDirs extension point used correctly for both ledger and standalone suites; follows the extensible targets pattern established by WP-007–WP-009.
da_file_name values in all 9 ledger YAMLs follow the N-<role-slug>.md pattern, consistent with cc_file_name. Correctly omitted from _shared.yaml (persona-specific field).
Standalone deep-agents files use content-basename filenames (no da_file_name in standalone YAMLs) — correct per WP scope.

Pre-existing ID anomaly (ledger-5-reviewer, ledger-6-docs, ledger-7-synthesis for personas 6, 8, 9) surfaces in deep-agents name fields but predates this WP and does not affect build correctness or the acceptance criteria.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. FRONTMATTER_DA is minimal, purposeful, and follows the extensible targets pattern. The config comment block explaining {{id}} for name (machine-readable) and {{cc_description}} dual-context behavior is the right call and prevents future misuse.

[documentation-forward] personas manifest (ai-insights personas/docs/ and personas-builder docs/agents/project-manifest/api-surface.md) should document: (1) the new da_file_name metadata field — purpose, naming convention (N-<role-slug>.md for ledger), and why standalone omits it; (2) the FRONTMATTER_DA convention of using {{id}} for name (machine-readable identifier for headless consumers) rather than {{name}} (human-readable title); (3) the cc_description dual-context resolution: ledger plugin roster-computed for ledger personas, YAML description field for standalone personas.

Pre-existing ID anomaly in 6-reviewer.yaml (id: ledger-5-reviewer), 8-documentation.yaml (id: ledger-6-docs), 9-synthesis.yaml (id: ledger-7-synthesis): these non-sequential IDs surface as the `name` field in deep-agents output, making the sequence appear as 1,2,3,4,5,5,6,7,7 to headless consumers. The da_file_name values are correctly sequential regardless. A housekeeping WP to align these YAML id fields with their sequence numbers would improve deep-agents discoverability.

summary: Updated personas/docs/agents/project-manifest/api-surface.md: added targets and frontmatter fields to the top-level config table; added outputDirs to the suite config table; added da_file_name field to the Per-Persona YAML Ledger Suite schema; updated {{cc_description}} computed variable to document dual-context resolution (ledger roster vs. standalone YAML description); added target_deep_agents column to the Platform Feature Flags table; added FRONTMATTER_DA section under Generated Frontmatter Templates explaining the {{id}}-for-name convention and cc_description dual-context behavior.

Updated personas/docs/agents/project-manifest/constraints.md: extended constraint 1 (never-edit generated files) to include the deep-agents directories for both suites; added personas/ledger/deep-agents/ and personas/standalone/deep-agents/ rows to the directory layout table; updated constraint 6 (naming) to cover the da_file_name field, its N-<role-slug>.md pattern, and the intentional omission from standalone YAMLs.

All three documentation-forward items from the Reviewer addressed: (1) da_file_name field spec and naming convention — documented in api-surface.md schema table and constraints.md constraint 6; (2) FRONTMATTER_DA {{id}}-for-name convention — documented in new FRONTMATTER_DA section with rationale; (3) cc_description dual-context resolution — documented in updated computed variables table.

comments.note: The pre-existing ID anomaly (ledger personas 6, 8, 9 having non-sequential ids: ledger-5-reviewer, ledger-6-docs, ledger-7-synthesis) surfaces in deep-agents name fields via {{id}}. Flagged by Developer, QA, and Reviewer — not in scope for this WP but worth a housekeeping pass to align IDs with sequence numbers in a future WP.

notes: All 4 acceptance criteria are met. The build produces 81 files (27 per target) with no warnings. Check that the deep-agents frontmatter (name from {{id}}, description from {{cc_description}}) is acceptable to QA — the ledger plugin computes cc_description from the roster, so ledger persona descriptions like 'Chief Product Officer — Planning & Strategy' appear in the deep-agents output correctly.

The standalone deep-agents files use content-basename filenames (e.g. developer.md) since no da_file_name was added to standalone YAMLs — this is intentional per WP scope. QA may want to verify this is acceptable or flag it as a follow-up.

All 4 AC verified and PASS. Build succeeds with 81 files across 3 targets; deep-agents output is minimal (name + description only); da_file_name naming is consistent. Note for Reviewer: the pre-existing ID anomalies in 6-reviewer, 8-documentation, 9-synthesis are worth a cleanup but out of scope for this WP.

All 4 AC confirmed. Implementation is clean and well-scoped. One documentation-forward item: the personas manifest docs should capture da_file_name field spec, the {{id}}-for-name convention in FRONTMATTER_DA, and cc_description dual-context resolution. Pre-existing ID anomaly (personas 6/8/9 have non-sequential ids) surfaces in deep-agents name output — harmless but worth a housekeeping pass in a future WP.
